sections.heading: Our Cosmic Neighborhood
sections.text: The solar system is made up of the Sun and everything that orbits around it. This includes 8 major planets, dwarf planets like Pluto, dozens of moons, millions of rocky asteroids, and icy comets wandering from the deep outer freeze.
keyPoints: The Sun contains 99.8% of all mass in the solar system.
Planets travel in elliptical orbits held by gravity.

sections.heading: The Inner Terrestrial Planets
sections.text: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars are the four inner planets. They are called terrestrial planets because they have solid, rocky surfaces. Earth is the only known world with oceans of liquid water and abundant life.
keyPoints: Mercury has extreme temperatures with no atmosphere to insulate it.
Venus has a thick atmosphere that traps heat like a giant greenhouse.
Mars has iron-rich red soil and polar ice caps.

sections.heading: The Outer Gas & Ice Giants
sections.text: Past the asteroid belt lie the giant planets: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Jupiter and Saturn are mostly hydrogen and helium gas, while Uranus and Neptune contain water, ammonia, and methane ice crystals giving them vivid blue hues.
keyPoints: Jupiter is so massive that all other planets could fit inside it.
Saturn features dazzling rings made of billions of ice chunks and dust.

lessons.title: Photosynthesis & Plant Cell Architecture
lessons.subject: Biology
lessons.description: Discover how chlorophyll converts sunlight, water, and CO2 into vital energy and oxygen.
lessons.author: Curriculum Team
lessons.videoTitle: Photosynthesis in 3D: Light Reaction & Calvin Cycle

pptSlides.title: Energy Capture in Chloroplasts
bullets: Thylakoid membranes hold green chlorophyll pigments

Byproduct released: Oxygen (O2) that all animals breathe
pptSlides.visualCue: Cross-section diagram of a plant leaf and chloroplast organelle

pptSlides.title: Chemical Equation of Life
bullets: Glucose provides metabolic fuel and structural cellulose for plant stems
Stomata pores open and close to regulate gas exchange and water conservation
pptSlides.visualCue: Balanced molecular diagram showing carbon atoms flowing into glucose rings

sections.heading: The Solar-Powered Cell
sections.text: Every green leaf is a miniature solar-powered biochemical factory. Through microscopic pores called stomata, leaves absorb carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil.
keyPoints: Chlorophyll pigments absorb blue and red light while reflecting green.
Solar energy splits water into oxygen and hydrogen protons.

sections.heading: Creating Glucose and Storing Fuel
sections.text: During the Calvin cycle, hydrogen combines with carbon dioxide to synthesize glucose sugars. This organic energy fuels cellular growth and forms the cellulose building blocks of trees and flora.
keyPoints: Plants store excess energy as starch granules.
Forests act as global carbon sinks regulating Earth's atmosphere.

quizQuestions.question: What central body sits at the very center of our solar system?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Sun is the yellow dwarf star at the center, providing light and gravity to keep all eight planets in stable orbits.

quizQuestions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mars appears reddish-orange because its surface minerals are rich in iron oxide (rust).

quizQuestions.question: Which is the largest planet in our entire solar system?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets in the solar system combined.

quizQuestions.question: What region separates the inner rocky planets from the outer gas giants?
quizQuestions.explanation: The main Asteroid Belt is located roughly between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.

quizQuestions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and completes an orbit in just 88 Earth days.

quizQuestions.question: What green pigment in plant cells captures sunlight for photosynthesis?
quizQuestions.explanation: Chlorophyll molecules inside chloroplasts absorb light photons to power chemical reactions.

quizQuestions.question: What gas do plants take in through leaf stomata to produce glucose?
quizQuestions.explanation: Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the surrounding air through tiny pores called stomata.

quizQuestions.question: What vital gas is released as a byproduct of splitting water during photosynthesis?
quizQuestions.explanation: When sunlight energizes chloroplasts to split H2O molecules, oxygen gas is released into the atmosphere.

submissions.audioTranscript: Hello Ms. Priya, this is Sam recording my voice response. The Goldilocks habitable zone for TRAPPIST-1e is much closer in than Earth is to the Sun because the red dwarf star is cooler and less luminous. Because of this tight orbit, tidal locking could occur, meaning one side always faces the star while the other faces deep space, requiring atmospheric winds to distribute warmth evenly.

teacherFeedback.suggestion: Superb explanation of tidal locking, Sam! For next time, consider explaining how strong atmospheric winds balance the hot and cold sides.
teacherFeedback.strengths: Deep astronomical understanding and clear, calm delivery.
